record.context_brief: Tail asymptotics for two-server queue at rho=1
record.original_question: In the two-server queue case m = 2 with stationary waiting time D, when the load satisfies rho = 1 and the service-time distribution is subexponential (for example regularly varying), what is the asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x becomes large?

evidence.quote: Again let D be the stationary waiting time. We formulate the following questions: what may the asymptotics for P(D > x) be when x is large and what is the typical sample path which lead to such a large value of the stationary waiting time.

The open problems here are (I formulate them in the particular case of a two server queue, m = 2): find the asymptotics for P(D > x) (i) if rho = 1 - at least, for some particular subexponential (say, regularly varying) distribution of service times;

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a FCFS queueing system with $m=2$ identical servers fed by a single renewal arrival stream with i.i.d. interarrival times $\{T_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ having mean $1/\lambda \in (0,\infty)$, and i.i.d. service times $\{S_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ (independent of $\{T_n\}$) with common distribution $B$ having finite mean $\mathbb{E}S_1 = 1/\mu$. Define the traffic intensity $\rho = \lambda/(m\mu) = \lambda/(2\mu)$, and assume the system admits a stationary waiting-time distribution; let $D$ denote the stationary waiting time of a typical customer (the time the customer spends in the queue before service begins).

Assume the service-time distribution $B$ is subexponential, meaning $\overline{B}(x):=1-B(x)>0$ for all $x$ and $\overline{B^{*2}}(x)/\overline{B}(x)\to 2$ as $x\to\infty$, where $B^{*2}$ is the two-fold convolution of $B$. As a representative concrete subclass, one may take $B$ regularly varying at infinity, i.e. $\overline{B}(x) = x^{-\alpha} L(x)$ for some $\alpha>1$ and slowly varying $L$.

Consider the critical-load case $\rho=1$. Determine the asymptotic behavior of $\mathbb{P}(D > x)$ as $x \to \infty$, and identify the typical sample path leading to a large value of the stationary waiting time $D$. In particular, provide explicit asymptotics in the case where $B$ is regularly varying.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has addressed the critical (half-loaded) GI/GI/2 case with regularly varying service times. Notably, Blanchet–Chen–Lam (2015, Queueing Systems) "Tail Asymptotics for Delay in a Half-loaded GI/GI/2 Queue with Heavy-tailed Job Sizes" provides asymptotic bounds and identifies two qualitative regimes (finite vs. infinite variance) for the tail of $\mathbb{P}(D>x)$, identifying typical-path behavior (one extremely big job vs. two moderately big jobs). The bounds are tight up to slowly varying factors in the finite-variance regime, while sharp asymptotics with explicit constants for general subexponential $B$ at $\rho=1$ remain incomplete; the broader subexponential (non–regularly varying) case at $\rho=1$ is largely unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Tail Asymptotics for Delay in a Half-loaded GI/GI/2 Queue with Heavy-tailed Job Sizes
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic bounds for the tail distribution of steady-state waiting time are obtained in a two-server queue where each server processes incoming jobs at a rate equal to the rate of their arrivals (half-loaded regime).
status_evidence.claim: Critical-load (rho=1) GI/GI/2 with regularly varying service times: tail bounds for P(D>x) and identification of typical-path regimes are established.

status_evidence.title: Queue length asymptotics for the multiple-server queue with heavy-tailed Weibull service times
status_evidence.snippet: Most results focus on regularly varying service times; the case of other heavy-tailed service times is poorly understood.
status_evidence.claim: Beyond regularly varying tails the multi-server heavy-tailed problem remains largely open.
